$comment: The demo catalogue: what the shop shows when no store is connected (src/data/shop/store.json has no domain). Same shape the store loader produces, the seed script sends and the test store serves. Prices in GBP. Every product is invented.

collections.title: Coats and jackets
collections.description: Nine coats and jackets in undyed wool, waxed cotton and linen. Forty of each, cut by hand.

image.altText: An older woman in the light putty trench walks down pale steps with the arch's shadow across her.

collections.title: Knitwear
collections.description: Ganseys, polos and a rollneck, knitted in the Borders and finished in the workroom.

image.altText: The oat rib polo folded on a stone ledge in low sun.

collections.title: Trousers
collections.description: Three trousers, all of them wide or straight, none of them tight.

image.altText: A man in wide oat trousers and a navy gansey walks along the quay.

products.title: Field coat
products.description: A plain field coat in undyed Shetland wool, cut long and straight so it hangs from the shoulders, not the waist. The wool keeps the colour of the sheep it came from, which is why no two runs are quite the same. The liner jacket buttons into it in January. Undyed Shetland wool, woven in the Borders Horn buttons, a single back vent Cut and sewn in the workroom in Marrowby, forty of each size Brush it, air it, and have it cleaned once a year at most
products.descriptionHtml:
A plain field coat in undyed Shetland wool, cut long and straight so it hangs from the shoulders, not the waist. The wool keeps the colour of the sheep it came from, which is why no two runs are quite the same.

The liner jacket buttons into it in January.

  • Undyed Shetland wool, woven in the Borders
  • Horn buttons, a single back vent
  • Cut and sewn in the workroom in Marrowby, forty of each size
  • Brush it, air it, and have it cleaned once a year at most

seo.title: Field coat — undyed Shetland wool
seo.description: A long, straight field coat in undyed Shetland wool, made in a run of forty in the workroom in Marrowby.

images.altText: The field coat in undyed wool, on a wooden hanger against a sunlit wall.
A woman in the field coat, worn open, walks along the foot of a sunlit wall.

products.title: Car coat
products.description: A short car coat in boiled wool, dyed rust. The colour took eleven tries to get right: the first ten were too orange, too brown, or too pleased with themselves. Boiled wool is knitted, then shrunk until it is dense enough to keep out wind. It doesn't fray, so the edges are left raw. Boiled merino wool, dyed rust Raw edges, three buttons, two deep pockets Cut and sewn in Marrowby, forty of each size Air it; it rarely needs cleaning

  • Raw edges, three buttons, two deep pockets

  • Air it; it rarely needs cleaning

seo.title: Car coat — boiled wool, rust
seo.description: A short car coat in rust boiled wool with raw edges, made in a run of forty.

images.altText: A woman in the rust car coat looks over her shoulder at the low sun.
A woman in a long rust coat stands against a sunlit harbour wall, her shadow across it.

products.title: Wrap coat
products.description: A long wrap coat with no buttons. It is tied, and it stays tied. Double-faced wool means two cloths woven together, so the coat has no lining and no inside to speak of. The edges are hand-finished: each one takes most of a day. Double-faced wool, bone Unlined, hand-finished edges, a self belt Cut and sewn in Marrowby, forty of each size Hang it on a broad hanger; steam out creases

seo.title: Wrap coat — double-faced wool, bone
seo.description: A long, unlined wrap coat in bone double-faced wool with hand-finished edges.

images.altText: An older woman in the long belted bone wrap coat stands side-on to a wall.
An older woman with a silver bob, wrapped in the pale wool coat, leans on the corner of a sunlit wall.

products.title: Overcoat
products.description: A black overcoat in heavy melton, the felted wool that navy coats were once made from. It is cut generously enough to go over a gansey and still close. It is the darkest thing we make, and the plainest. Wool melton, black Half-lined in cotton, four horn buttons Cut and sewn in Marrowby, forty of each size Brush after wearing; clean once a year at most

seo.title: Overcoat — melton, black
seo.description: A plain black overcoat in heavy wool melton, cut to go over knitwear.

images.altText: A man in the long black overcoat with a pale scarf stands against the wall as the sun drops.

products.title: Smock
products.description: An over-the-head smock in olive waxed cotton. It goes darker where you hold it and paler where the sun lands, and after a year it looks like yours. A half placket, a deep front pocket, a hood that folds into the collar. Waxed cotton, olive Half placket, kangaroo pocket, folding hood Cut and sewn in Marrowby, forty of each size Wipe it clean; re-wax it every second winter

images.altText: A man in the olive waxed-cotton smock sits on a stone bollard by the wall, his hands in his pockets.

products.title: Raincoat
products.description: A long raincoat in waxed linen. Linen is lighter than cotton and creases like paper; waxed, it keeps off the kind of rain that comes sideways off the sea. A collar that turns up and stays up. Waxed linen, ink Storm collar, raglan sleeves, deep pockets Cut and sewn in Marrowby, forty of each size Wipe it clean; never wash it

images.altText: An older woman in the long dark waxed-linen raincoat, collar turned up, stands in a strip of sun.

products.title: Liner jacket
products.description: A quilted liner that buttons into the field coat in January and goes out on its own in May. Sold out for this season; the next run is cut in the spring. Diamond quilting in cotton thread, a wool wadding that stays warm when it is damp. Cotton shell, wool wadding, putty Buttons into the field coat Cut and sewn in Marrowby, forty of each size Wash cool, dry flat

seo.title: Liner jacket — quilted cotton, putty
seo.description: A quilted putty liner jacket that buttons into the field coat or goes out alone.

images.altText: A woman in the short quilted putty jacket sits on the edge of the quay wall.

products.title: Linen jacket
products.description: A jacket in linen heavy enough to keep its shape in a sea wind. Three patch pockets, no lining, and a collar that sits flat whether or not you want it to. It softens with every wash and creases from the first wearing. Both are the point. Heavy linen, oat Unlined, three patch pockets Cut and sewn in Marrowby, forty of each size Wash cool; hang to dry

seo.title: Linen jacket — heavy linen, oat
seo.description: An unlined oat linen jacket with patch pockets, heavy enough to hold its shape.

images.altText: Someone in the matching oat linen jacket and trousers stands in a plastered archway.
Someone in the loose oat linen jacket sits on pale plaster steps, face turned into the sun.

products.title: Trench
products.description: An unlined trench in putty cotton gabardine, for a summer that keeps not arriving. No epaulettes, no gun flap, no D-rings: the parts of a trench that were for something else. It packs small and comes out of the bag looking as if it meant to. Cotton gabardine, putty Unlined, raglan sleeves, a self belt Cut and sewn in Marrowby, forty of each size Wash cool; hang to dry

products.title: Gansey
products.description: A fisherman's gansey knitted in the round, so it has no side seams to give way. The band of stitches across the chest is the pattern of one harbour; every harbour had its own. Tight enough to keep the wind out, loose enough to go under the overcoat. Five-ply worsted wool Knitted in the round, gusseted underarms Knitted in the Borders, finished in Marrowby Hand wash, dry flat

seo.description: A fisherman's gansey knitted in the round in worsted wool, in navy or ecru.

images.altText: The navy gansey laid flat on unbleached linen, its stitch pattern caught by low light.
A man in the olive smock over an ecru gansey sits on a stone bollard.
A man in the navy gansey carries a folded coat over one arm along the quay.

products.title: Rib polo
products.description: A ribbed polo in lambswool with a deep collar that stands up under a coat and lies flat without one. It goes under everything we make, which is why there are two colours of it.
